title: Impact of School Finance Reform on Math Test Scores

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy
Difference-in-Differences (DID) is the appropriate method here. We have a treatment group (schools affected by finance reform) and control group (unaffected schools) observed before and after the reform implementation. The key identifying assumption is parallel trends - that treated and control schools would have had similar trajectories in math test scores in the absence of the reform. This allows us to use the control group to estimate the counterfactual outcome for treated schools.

## 2. R Code
```r
# Load necessary libraries
library(readr)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(broom)

# Read the data
data <- read_csv("experiments/exp_b/data/s35_data.csv")

# Basic data exploration
print("Data summary:")
print(summary(data))

# Check treatment assignment
print("Treatment distribution:")
print(table(data$treated, data$post))

# Main DID regression
did_model <- lm(y ~ treated + post + treat_x_post, data = data)

print("Main DID Results:")
print(summary(did_model))

# Extract the treatment effect
treatment_effect <- coef(did_model)["treat_x_post"]
se_treatment <- summary(did_model)$coefficients["treat_x_post", "Std. Error"]
p_value <- summary(did_model)$coefficients["treat_x_post", "Pr(>|t|)"]

print(paste("Treatment Effect (ATE):", round(treatment_effect, 4)))
print(paste("Standard Error:", round(se_treatment, 4)))
print(paste("P-value:", round(p_value, 4)))

# Robustness check: Include unit fixed effects
did_fe <- lm(y ~ factor(unit_id) + post + treat_x_post, data = data)

print("Robustness Check - With Unit Fixed Effects:")
treatment_effect_fe <- coef(did_fe)["treat_x_post"]
se_treatment_fe <- summary(did_fe)$coefficients["treat_x_post", "Std. Error"]

print(paste("Treatment Effect with FE:", round(treatment_effect_fe, 4)))
print(paste("Standard Error with FE:", round(se_treatment_fe, 4)))

# Visual check for parallel trends (pre-treatment periods)
pre_treatment <- data %>% filter(post == 0)
means_by_period <- pre_treatment %>% 
  group_by(period, treated) %>% 
  summarise(mean_y = mean(y), .groups = 'drop')

print("Pre-treatment means by group and period:")
print(means_by_period)

# Simple visualization of treatment effect
group_means <- data %>%
  group_by(treated, post) %>%
  summarise(mean_y = mean(y), .groups = 'drop') %>%
  mutate(group = ifelse(treated == 1, "Treated", "Control"),
         period = ifelse(post == 1, "Post", "Pre"))

print("Group means for DID visualization:")
print(group_means)

# Calculate the difference-in-differences manually as verification
treated_diff <- group_means$mean_y[group_means$group == "Treated" & group_means$period == "Post"] - 
                group_means$mean_y[group_means$group == "Treated" & group_means$period == "Pre"]

control_diff <- group_means$mean_y[group_means$group == "Control" & group_means$period == "Post"] - 
                group_means$mean_y[group_means$group == "Control" & group_means$period == "Pre"]

manual_did <- treated_diff - control_diff

print(paste("Manual DID calculation:", round(manual_did, 4)))
print(paste("Regression DID coefficient:", round(treatment_effect, 4)))
```

## 3. Expected Findings
I expect a positive treatment effect of approximately 0.2-0.4 standard deviations. School finance reforms typically increase per-pupil spending in treated districts, which should translate to improved educational resources, smaller class sizes, better teacher quality, and enhanced learning materials. These improvements generally lead to modest but meaningful gains in test scores. The magnitude should be economically significant (around 0.3 SD is considered a meaningful educational intervention effect) but not extremely large, as educational improvements take time to materialize and face various implementation challenges.

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: We compare changes in math test scores over time between schools affected by the reform and those that were not.
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: The reform led to a decrease in math test scores.
